tip: гораздо (gorazdo = much) intensifies a comparative: гораздо интереснее (gorazdo interesnee = much more interesting).

english: Friends are more important than work.
tip: After a comparative, the thing compared goes in the genitive: важнее работы (vazhnee raboty = more important than work).

english: My father works as a doctor.
tip: работать (rabotat = to work) plus the instrumental names a job: работает врачом (rabotaet vrachom = works as a doctor).
Numbers 2, 3, 4 take a genitive singular noun: три комнаты (tri komnaty = three rooms), not the plural form.

target: Он такой же высокий, как брат.
english: He is as tall as his brother.
tip: For equal comparison use такой же ... как (takoy zhe ... kak = as ... as): такой же высокий (takoy zhe vysokiy = just as tall).

target: Книга, которую я читаю, очень интересная.
english: The book that I am reading is very interesting.
tip: которую (kotoruyu = that/which) is feminine accusative here, matching книга (kniga = book) as the object being read.

target: Для того чтобы успеть, нужно встать рано.
english: In order to make it, you need to get up early.
tip: With one subject, чтобы (chtoby = in order to) takes the infinitive: чтобы успеть (chtoby uspet = in order to make it).

target: Не сдавайся, ты уже почти достиг своей цели!
english: Don't give up, you've almost reached your goal!
tip: Negative commands take the imperfective verb: Не сдавайся (Ne sdavaysya = don't give up), not the perfective form.

english: She is stronger than she looks.
tip: When the comparison is a whole clause, use чем (chem = than): сильнее, чем выглядит (silnee, chem vyglyadit = stronger than she looks).

english: He is a more experienced doctor.
tip: более (bolee = more) plus a plain adjective forms a comparative: более опытный (bolee opytnyy = more experienced).

english: The eldest brother is the tallest.
tip: самый (samyy = most) before an adjective builds the superlative: самый высокий (samyy vysokiy = the tallest).

target: Сядьте поудобнее, мы начинаем нашу презентацию.
english: Make yourselves comfortable. We're starting our presentation.
tip: The по- prefix on a comparative softens it to 'a bit more': поудобнее (poudobnee = a bit more comfortable).

target: Он бегает быстрее всех в классе.
english: He runs faster than everyone in the class.
tip: A comparative plus всех (vsekh = than all) means best of the group: быстрее всех (bystree vsekh = faster than everyone).

target: Чем дальше в лес, тем больше дров.
english: The further into the forest, the more firewood.
tip: The frame Чем ... тем ... (chem ... tem ... = the more ... the more) links two comparatives: Чем дальше, тем больше (chem dalshe, tem bolshe).

english: He speaks Russian better than me.
tip: по-русски (po-russki = in Russian) is the set adverb for speaking a language: говорит по-русски (govorit po-russki = speaks Russian).

target: Позаботьтесь о домашних животных, пока меня нет.
english: Take care of the pets while I'm away.
tip: To say someone is absent, use нет plus the genitive: меня нет (menya net = I'm not here, I'm away).
Many comparatives change their last stem sound: короткий becomes короче (korotkiy to koroche = shorter), the к turning into ч.
уже (uzhe = narrower) looks exactly like уже meaning already; stress and context tell the two apart.
лучше (luchshe = better) is the irregular comparative of хороший (khoroshiy = good), not a regular ending you can predict.
A possessive matches the noun, not you: книга (kniga = book) is feminine, so my is моя (moya), not мой (moy).
место (mesto = seat) is neuter, so your becomes твоё (tvoyo); masculine would be твой (tvoy), feminine твоя (tvoya).
Её (yeyo = her), его (yego = his), их (ikh = their) never change form, unlike мой (moy) or наш (nash): Её платье (platye = dress) keeps Её.
The ending -ся/-сь means it happened on its own: машина (mashina = car) сломалась (slomalas = broke down), nobody broke it.
готов (gotov = ready) is a short adjective for a state, and Russian adds no word for is: заказ готов (zakaz gotov = order ready).
After a comparative you can drop than and put the noun in genitive: теплее весны (teplee vesny = warmer than spring), весна (vesna) becoming весны.
Use свой (svoy) when the owner is the subject: Я взял свою книгу (ya vzyal svoyu knigu = I took my own book), not мою (moyu).
свой (svoy) means his own here because he is the subject; using его (yego) would hint the passport belongs to someone else.
With нравится (nravitsya = likes), the person goes in dative: Моему другу (moyemu drugu), and музыка (muzyka) is the grammatical subject.
самый (samyy = most) before an adjective builds the superlative and agrees in gender: самый умный ученик (samyy umnyy uchenik = smartest student).
Use чем (chem = than) to compare against an adverb: счастливее (schastlivee = happier), чем раньше (ranshe = before).
